title: Evening screens
tomorrow: two angels walk you home on Friday night. what do they look for?

lines: WHEN YOU SLEEP, PUT IT OUT.
cards: Phones now come with a bedtime mode that turns the screen amber and quiet. The idea is older than electricity.
In Medina, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, gave the people a short list for nightfall, and it ends with the light.

Once, after a house in the city caught fire in the night, he said: this fire is an enemy to you, so when you go to sleep, put it out. In the hadith, the lamp has a wick: a small flame, burning beside the people it lit.

teach.h: CLOSE THE DOOR, SAY GOD'S NAME.
teach.b: His companion Jabir remembered the whole list, and every item is something your hands do. When night falls, bring the children in. Close the door, and say God's name.
Tie up the water-skin, and say God's name.
Cover the dishes, even if all you have is a stick to lay across them, and say God's name.
And put out the lamps when you sleep, he said, because the little mischief-maker, the mouse, may drag the wick and burn down the house.

Listen to it as sound: the latch clicking, the lid set on the pot, the small hiss of a flame pinched out, and then the dark. In Islam these belong to the manners of the night, part of the sunnah, the Prophet's way.
Two things make them more than safety tips.

Each chore is done with bismillah, in the name of God, so closing the house becomes a kind of remembrance. And the list ends in darkness on purpose: the day is over, the house is shut, nothing is left burning by the bed.
Our lamps don't drip oil. They glow, and buzz, and pull. The old manners still ask the same question: when does the light go out?

how: Muslims learn the Prophet's manners of nightfall from hadith: closing the doors, covering food and water and putting out lamps before sleep, saying bismillah with each.

practice: Get up and close your house for the night: shut one door, cover one glass, and turn off one light, or set your phone face down across the room.
If you're Muslim, say bismillah with each one; if not, say softly what you're doing as you do it. Then sit in the dimmer room and listen to it.

wordCard.voice: Evening screens: choosing when tonight's light goes out, the way the Prophet's night manners end with the lamps put out before sleep.

orig.note: Arabic: in the name of God, said with each chore of closing the house.

carryVoice: Keep this one: screens off, the last chore of a house closed for the night. Sleep well.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3280 (Jabir: when night falls keep the children in; close the doors, tie the water-skins, cover the vessels and put out the lamps, mentioning God's name)
